body:
Founder real-time: "i need an okemily manifest text file on the server that serves all blog posts
as a single text file with norobots." (Refined from an earlier, broader "manifest" ask that turned
out to mean something different -- a repo-file index built as a GitHub Actions artifact, built
separately in OKEMILY/.github/workflows/repo-manifest.yml + scripts/generate_repo_manifest.py.)

New Renderer.RenderManifest (internal/blog/render.go) writes every post's full plain-text content,
newest-first, into one file at OutputDir's parent (/var/www/okemily/blog-manifest.txt, alongside
OutputDir=/var/www/okemily/blog). Wired into both the live publish path
(handlers/blog.go's Create, same place RenderIndex already runs) and cmd/blog-rerender (backfill
tool) so it never drifts from the DB.

Real bug found and fixed along the way, the hard way: okemily-deploy.sh's rsync --delete wiped
the manifest immediately after first generating it, because it lives at the OKEMILY repo's static
root but isn't part of that repo (server-rendered, not tracked) -- the exact same failure mode the
script's own header already documents for blog/ and tyler/ (a real prior incident, 2026-07-19).
Added the missing --exclude='blog-manifest.txt'.

robots.txt added to OKEMILY (Disallow: /blog-manifest.txt) -- the founder's own "norobots" ask,
to avoid a duplicate-content SEO penalty against the individually-indexed blog post pages.

Verified live, not just built: go build/go test clean, IDUNA restarted, manifest regenerated (156
posts, 490KB) and confirmed to survive a second deploy run, robots.txt and blog-manifest.txt both
return real HTTP 200 at https://okemily.com/.
title: Blog manifest text file: live at okemily.com/blog-manifest.txt, robots-excluded
